leftEvidence.title: A parent tells a child why the annual unleavened service is kept

points.label: Repetition
points.left: The ordinance is kept in its season from year to year.
points.right: Jesus’s parents go every year according to feast custom.

points.label: Child and parent
points.left: The parent supplies an explanation to a son.
points.right: Parents search, question, hear an answer, and do not understand it.

points.label: Place
points.left: The command anticipates life in the promised land.
points.right: The family travels from Nazareth to Jerusalem and back.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus’s parents go yearly to Jerusalem, where his temple saying is not understood and later remembered

payload.tension: One source commands intergenerational explanation; the other narrates a family observance whose central saying remains uncomprehended.
payload.title: Children ask and a family keeps Passover
